timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed CLI stream source 1; it is transport-only in the ledger with 0 semantic events out of 6380 source events.
Reviewed serial main trajectory: black-box probing, file writes, build, differential tests, argv fix, final response, no delegation.

parallel.requirements: Port the provided C++ URL parser driver to pure Rust 2021 with zero external crates, matching CLI arguments, stdout bytes, and /output artifact placement by black-box inference from test16_executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent launched a wide workflow for behavioral characterization, refutation, and spec synthesis, but the parent itself retained ownership of implementation, assembly, build, and differential verification.
parallel.implementation: The parent locally probed symbols and behavior, wrote url_parser modules plus test16.rs and Cargo.toml, handled parser validators/path behavior, and adjusted the differential harness while the workflow ran.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final /output tree contained Cargo.toml, test16.rs, executable test16, and library modules; artifact validation accepted the directory even though final.txt was empty.
parallel.verification: The parent compiled with rustc and cargo, ran unit tests, ran a 47,715-case differential fuzzer and a 408,476-case larger fuzz run, then official evaluation passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The auxiliary workflow ended killed with null aggregate result, one 429 child error, and progress children; the agent process timed out after artifact completion, with no evaluator-visible defect.

serial.requirements: The serial run worked from the same prompt: pure Rust 2021, zero crates, /output Cargo project, byte-for-byte CLI/output behavior, and black-box inference from the compiled C++ binary.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With workflows disabled and delegation tools denied, one main agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final reporting.
serial.implementation: The serial agent discovered the header/source absence, used binary symbols and probes to infer parse, scheme, host, port, path, and output behavior, wrote the Cargo project, and fixed non-UTF-8 argv handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact validation found Cargo.toml, test16.rs, executable test16, and url_parser modules in the final tree, with expected entry test16.rs and ok true.
serial.verification: The serial run built with rustc and cargo, ran curated, exhaustive, fuzz, raw-byte, and final suites, reported 23,568 zero-mismatch cases, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No required task behavior is shown unresolved; the final note says encode.rs was not differentially exercised because test16 did not call it, while tested program behavior passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run received and recognized the pure Rust, zero-dependency, /output Cargo-project, black-box URL parser requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the identical prompt and recognized the same black-box porting and byte-for-byte output obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference; both targeted the same CLI behavior and artifact shape.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent delegated broad characterization, refutation, and spec synthesis while retaining direct implementation ownership in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had workflows and delegation denied and handled probing, implementation, and verification in one main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split research across many children but did not delegate implementation ownership; serial was a single-agent control.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow briefs gave children the binary, C++ driver behavior, known facts, and dimension-specific probing tasks; parent also probed key facts locally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run derived the missing header/library semantics from symbols and direct binary probes before coding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more handoff surface, but no lost or conflicting context is tied to a bad deliverable; serial had no child handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent wrote a multi-module Rust implementation, built it, fixed warnings, and adjusted behavior after probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote the analogous Cargo project and fixed a non-UTF-8 argv divergence after differential testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the same observable parser behavior; file organization differed slightly but both artifacts satisfied the task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow aggregate ended killed with null result and several child states unfinished, while the parent artifact was already present.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial trajectory ended normally with a final response after builds and differential tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an incomplete auxiliary workflow lifecycle; serial had a clean single-agent closure. The incomplete workflow did not prevent accepted delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implementation writes were performed by the parent into the final /output tree; protocol checks report delegation use but no contamination paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote and built a coherent final tree without subagents or shared-workspace handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No observed write collision, overwrite, or artifact leakage distinguished the accepted artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent ran local build/unit/differential tests, including a 408,476-case run, before the official 40/40 evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run ran curated, exhaustive, fuzz, raw-byte, and final verification suites before the official 40/40 evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong whole-task acceptance evidence; serial documented it in final text, parallel left it in trajectory/status records.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent 2,099,023 workflow-child tokens, reached the 2399-second timeout, and left the workflow killed with unfinished children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally in 997.704 agent seconds with no subagents and 1400 seconds remaining in retry metadata.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had much worse budget closure, but no unresolved required stage or failed official outcome resulted from it.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status.json evaluation records have solution_passed true and 40/40 testcases. The concrete difference is process-only: parallel used a broad workflow and timed out with the workflow killed, while serial completed normally without delegation. Because the parallel artifact was complete and officially accepted, that process closure problem did not create a retained task-solving failure.
parallel_contributors: Parent retained implementation and verification ownership despite launching a 32-agent characterization/refutation workflow.
Local differential testing and artifact creation completed before the process was killed at the timeout.
Official artifact validation and evaluator results confirm the delivered Rust tree was accepted.
serial_contributors: Single-agent probing and implementation avoided workflow lifecycle overhead.
Serial differential testing found and fixed the byte-oriented argv issue before normal completion.
Official artifact validation and evaluator results confirm the delivered Rust tree was accepted.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two implementations used slightly different module names and verification corpus sizes, but both matched the observable task sufficiently for the official tests.
Parallel final.txt was empty because the process was killed, while serial produced a written summary; the deliverable artifact, not final prose, determined the official outcome.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences are documented but not retained as concurrency-error consequences

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned and performed implementation writes in the main trajectory, so implementation was not unassigned.
There were not multiple child-owned implementations requiring an unowned merge; the parent assembled one coherent Rust tree.
The required Cargo project, test16.rs entry point, executable, and modules were present and artifact validation succeeded.
The parent covered probing, writing, building, differential verification, and artifact delivery despite the auxiliary workflow timeout.
The workflow was not a mandatory serial preflight; the parent independently probed and started implementation while it ran.
Parallel investigation and implementation overlapped; implementation was not deferred until the workflow completed, and the final artifact passed.
The indispensable implementation and verification path received enough parent attention to build and pass; auxiliary fan-out did not leave required work undone.
The workflow fan-out and timeout are direct evidence, but no required task work was displaced because a complete artifact passed 40/40.
Child scopes were dimension or refutation probes, and no single overbroad child owned indispensable implementation work left unfinished.
The workflow brief included the binary, driver, observable outputs, established facts, and dimension-specific probing instructions; no known omitted requirement made child work unusable.
Children produced research/spec findings rather than separately owned interoperating components, so no missing interface contract caused incompatible integration.
No evidence shows a known finding disappeared in transfer and forced repeated work; the parent used local probes and produced a passing implementation.
Although the workflow was broad, the parent did not leave a dependent implementation or acceptance action unfinished because returned information was too large.
No consumed child result is shown to describe a superseded workspace or requirement state causing invalid work.
The workflow contained corrections/refutations, but no unresolved conflict reached an integration decision and caused a blocked or wrong final artifact.
The parent did not rely only on workflow completion or file existence; it ran whole-program differential tests and the official evaluation passed with no visible acceptance gap.
Workflow children had internal stall retries, but no replacement or retry is shown repeating required work without inherited state and causing a deliverable consequence.

candidates.reason: The workflow was killed with active/progress children, but their unfinished work was not needed for a successful artifact, so the retention gate lacks an adverse task consequence.
No complete child candidate or compatible component set was left unpromoted; the final Rust tree already existed and passed artifact validation.
There is no visible child result merged after integrated verification; local differential tests covered the parent-built artifact.
No child completed a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve; implementation remained parent-owned.
Some verifier/refuter children were unfinished at kill, but no concrete needed finding was trapped below the parent before a failed or unverifiable closure.
One child hit a 429 workflow error, but the parent had already covered the task through its own probes/tests and no required failed child scope remained necessary.
No completed child result is shown as available, ignored, and then contradicted by parent action; the accepted artifact was consistent with verified behavior.
The parent waited on TaskOutput and timed out, but it had already checked the long fuzz result and completed the artifact; no available progress would have changed a missing required next action.
There is no evidence that live agents wrote competing files or overlapping implementation paths; child work was research/probing while parent wrote sources.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source/configuration file or reconciling concurrent same-file edits.
No agent replaced or wholesale rewrote non-entry source produced or owned by another live agent.
No child or concurrent actor overwrote the required entry point or executable; the parent-created deliverable validated successfully.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
The workflow involved many agents, but no concrete unstable state or provenance problem from shared implementation writes is visible.
Protocol/status records show no contamination path hits, and no generated concurrent artifact was consumed as a stable reference environment.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The killed workflow, unfinished children, 429 child error, TaskOutput wait, and timeout were treated as one closure chain and all rejected because the parent artifact had already passed local and official verification.

Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered together rather than multiplied around the same terminal workflow state.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no candidate met the adverse-consequence retention gate after both artifacts passed.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained for high child count, token use, timeout, or killed workflow alone because those were not tied to lost required work, bad integration, or failed acceptance.
